preconditions.description: The number of cities n and attacked cities m satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 123456.
There are exactly n - 1 edges describing the road system.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct cities within the valid range [1, n].
The list of attacked cities contains exactly m distinct integers.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= c <= n for c in attacked_cities)
preconditions.description: All attacked city numbers are within the valid range [1, n].
The graph formed by n cities and the given edges is a connected tree (n nodes, n-1 edges, connected).

postconditions.description: The output city number is a valid city index between 1 and n.
The minimum time is calculated as 2 * (number of attacked cities - 1) minus the maximum distance from the optimal start city to any attacked city.

postconditions.expression: max_dist_from_optimal == max(distance(optimal_city, target) for target in attacked_cities)
postconditions.description: The maximum distance used in the calculation is the longest shortest path from the optimal city to any attacked city.

postconditions.expression: all(min_time <= 2 * (len(attacked_cities) - 1) - max(distance(c, target) for target in attacked_cities) for c in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: The calculated min_time is the global minimum over all possible starting cities.

postconditions.expression: all(optimal_city <= c for c in range(1, n + 1) if 2 * (len(attacked_cities) - 1) - max(distance(c, target) for target in attacked_cities) == min_time)
postconditions.description: If multiple cities yield the same minimum time, the one with the smallest city number is chosen.
The output consists of exactly two lines: the optimal city number and the minimum time.
